value.body: An aviation ground instructor teaches the theory that student pilots must pass in DGCA exams: air navigation, meteorology, air regulations and aircraft technical subjects. Employers are flying training organisations and private ground schools that prepare students for CPL exams. Days are classroom-based, with lectures, practice tests and doubt sessions.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: A CPL, or passes in the DGCA CPL ground subjects, plus teaching ability

items.label: Subjects taught
items.value: Air Navigation, Meteorology, Air Regulations, Technical General/Specific

items.label: Flying training organisations
items.source: Lok Sabha reply, Ministry of Civil Aviation (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Newly licensed or CPL-exam-qualified pilots often join ground schools or flying training organisations as instructors while they wait for airline openings. A demo class is a common part of hiring.

value.title: At a glance
items: Often a bridge role while a pilot waits for an airline job.
Next roles: senior or chief ground instructor, or a move to flight instruction after the required ratings.
Pay and stability vary widely across schools.

competition.note: B.Sc (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education

women.note: Share of women among B.Sc (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 — the entry degree, not people already working in this role.
women.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
